text.name: TextDesc2
text.text: The Sharp MZ-700 was a home computer released in Japan in 1982 as part of Sharp's MZ series. Designed as a lower-cost successor to the MZ-80 series, it used a Zilog Z80A processor and focused on expandability, programming, and hobby computing. Unlike many competing computers of the era, the MZ-700 used a "clean computer" design where the operating system and programming languages were loaded from external media instead of being permanently stored in ROM. The system featured a simple but flexible graphics system, optional printer and plotter support, and compatibility with cassette-based software. The MZ-700 became popular among Japanese computer enthusiasts and helped establish Sharp's reputation in the home computer market.
